evidence: Judged DRAFT.txt (“Have you got any sense of what it is that's making it feel fake?”) against SOURCE.txt and CONTEXT.txt. It is Emulate's sample-co sentence exactly as the_change gives it; the_change names no AI fix or put-back, and the draft has none. CONTEXT.txt holds it once, as the first sentence under the heading “It feels fake”, followed by the unchanged “The words, an image, what you are expecting to get from this, a role you feel you have to play etc.” SOURCE.txt: the words replaced (not his own) are “Do you have a sense of what it is that feels fake?”, and the meaning to keep is his published guide's “First ask what feels fake: the wording, the image, the expectation, or the role you’re trying to perform.” Word by word: “Do you have a sense” becomes “Have you got any sense” (same ask; “any” invites even a faint sense, which is no change in strength; “Have you got” sits with the article's own “see how you get on”); “of what it is that” is unchanged; “feels fake” becomes “that's making it feel fake”, the one real difference, because the question moves from which part feels fake to what is making it feel fake. I judged that equivalent in use: the reader is asked to pinpoint the same thing, the four candidates that follow (words, image, expectation, role) are the guide's own and answer either wording, and the next sentences, which say it is not necessarily about lacking a grown-up voice, read at least as well against a cause. Nothing is added (no claim, condition, person or number) and nobody changes role (the reader does the noticing in both). Nothing of his is left out that the change says it puts back, since it says none; “First” is not in the replaced words and the question stays the item's opener. The writer's T14 and T15 lines say the sentence “puts back” a point Emulate dropped; for S30 that is boilerplate (the change is Emulate's sentence as written), and I judged the draft, not that line. T24 and T19: the question is followed at once by candidate answers, but that is the guide's own “ask what feels fake: the wording, the image…” shape and a question a reader with this problem would ask, not suspense or an announcement, so ABSENT. T02, T09, T13: the paragraph's cadence, reasons and asides are unchanged outside this one sentence. C02: “it” is the practice the heading names. All other rows ABSENT.
